obligations.note: The change sets payments.privileged_idle_minutes and PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES to 16, which is above the catalog bound of 15, so a privileged session can remain accepted after more than 15 idle minutes. EXC-0210 does not cure this: it is scoped to mortgage.session, and EXC-0141 (payments.session) expired on 2026-09-19, before the 2026-10-19 review.
Ticket CHG-24034 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components payments.policy and payments.controls-data cover policy.py and controls/payments/policy-params.json.
Mara Costa, a payments change approver and not the author Jonah Weiss, approved a code_review of commit 63831d63ea62571ff2cb852fe5ce1f85739d28d9.
The change is a single commit, and both the code_review and control_owner approvals name that head commit.

records/ci/run.json reports success for ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments on the head commit, and the JUnit report shows the full suite, including unskipped test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy, with 0 failures and 0 skipped.
controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path. Rachel Stein, a control_owner on the controls-office team (outside payments-eng), approved that commit.

The change relies on EXC-0210 for the SES-1 deviation, but that exception is for mortgage.session and Mortgage privileged sessions, not payments. The payments.session exception EXC-0141 is expired at review time, so no approved, in-scope, unexpired exception authorizes the 16-minute idle limit.

summary: The change raises Payments’s privileged idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes in both policy.py and the approved policy parameters. That violates SES-1, whose bound is at most 15 minutes. The cited exception EXC-0210 covers Mortgage sessions, not Payments, and the Payments session exception has expired. Process approvals, the ticket, and CI on the final commit are in order, but the idle-timeout deviation is not authorized, so the change is rejected.
